lens: HeroUI (formerly NextUI): soft, rounded, friendly consumer-grade polish with Framer Motion
name: Friendly Coach Studio
one_liner: A warm, rounded, motion-led training studio: a live coach rail beside every call, and a browsable persona library with an AI wizard, all shipped in the open-source core.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the HeroUI lens: soft rounded surfaces, friendly consumer polish, Tailwind-native components. Changed two points. First, HeroUI v3 (formerly NextUI) dropped its framer-motion dependency (GitHub discussion #6335), so Motion is added as a separate package for choreography instead of assuming the library provides it. Second, the palette uses a warm canvas and a violet coach accent instead of a default library blue, so the app does not read as another template. Self-score (1-10): A 8, B 8, C 7, D 6.5, E 6, F1 5, F2 6.5, F3 3 (on F3, 3 means worth building).

ui_stack.name: Motion (the former framer-motion package)

palette.use: Page background (warm paper), replaces the cool #F8FAFC
Cards, drawers and the transcript panel
Headings, body text, top bars and the dark debrief band
Coach Violet: primary CTAs and AI-sourced elements (5.4:1 on white)
Live coral-red: recording dot and End and grade button (4.7:1 with white text)
Mint fills and rings for on-track scores; use positive-text #137A50 for mint text (5.3:1)
Amber fills for nudges and objection alerts; always paired with ink text

design_language.typography: Bricolage Grotesque 600-700 for display and screen titles (replaces Sora); Inter 400-600 for UI and transcript; Geist Mono for timers, scores and timestamps. Base 16px with a scale of 14, 16, 20, 28, 40, 56.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 20px for cards, 14px for inputs, full pills for chips and the Voice/Text toggle. Two warm-tinted shadow levels only. 1px inner hairline borders. A 12px backdrop blur is used only on the live coach rail to separate it from the transcript.
design_language.motion: Springs (stiffness 300, damping 30) for whisper cards and drawers; layoutId shared-element morph from a library card into the persona header; score rings tween 600ms ease-out; the orb scale follows mic level. prefers-reduced-motion swaps all movement for opacity fades.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke with rounded caps. Persona avatars are generated industry glyph tiles (gradient plus icon), never photos, which avoids real-person likeness issues.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default and dark ships in v1 via the same tokens, switched by data-theme and following prefers-color-scheme. Dark values: canvas #0F1117, surface #171A24, ink #F4F5F8, primary lifted to #8B7CFF, positive text #35C489.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: a slim left rail with five items (Practice, Library, Progress, Team, Settings), a Cmd+K palette, and a persistent Create persona button in the top bar. Mobile: a bottom tab bar with the same items, hidden during a live call. Practice is the signed-in home screen; the marketing landing stays public at the root. Library is the entry point for every sales job, which retires today's three-item scenario dropdown. Settings holds model choice, voice provider, the org rubric and accessibility options.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Three lanes run in parallel and the UI shows each one. Persona lane: the voice or text caller, who never sees coaching. Coach lane: a small text model reads recent turns and the rubric and emits at most one whisper every 20 seconds (types: objection alert, next question, don't-say, talk-track step), each 12 words or fewer, with a 'why' link to the transcript line. Grader lane: streams rubric deltas after each rep turn, target under 1.5 seconds; live numbers are labeled 'live estimate' and update at turn end to avoid jitter. The debrief uses the same rubric and evidence rules, so live and final scores agree. Rep controls: intensity, mute coach, hotkeys, and a model swap for the coach and grader.
persona_library_and_wizard: Ship about 150 personas across 16+ sales jobs (SDR cold call, AE discovery, CS renewal, collections, recruiting, retail, solar, insurance, mortgage, real estate, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement), each with two or three scenarios. Every persona is a plain JSON or YAML file with job, industry, difficulty, objection tags, rubric template and voice, so community PRs can add whole packs. Filters are first-class in the UI. The AI wizard takes context from five source types, streams a draft into editable fields, proposes a rubric, runs a dry run, then saves locally or exports a PR-ready pack. Built-in personas ship only after review by a domain practitioner; unreviewed ones are labeled 'community draft'.
signature_moments: A violet whisper card slides in from the coach rail on a spring, and one tap uses its line.
Rubric rings tick and pulse mint only when the rep earns evidence, so progress is felt during the call.
A library card morphs into the persona header of the live call through a shared-element transition.
The debrief replay bar lets the rep scrub the call, with each scored moment lighting up in the transcript.
'Drill this moment' replays only the turn that cost points, for 60 seconds, from the same persona state.
The persona orb breathes with mic level in voice mode and falls back to a CSS gradient on phones and under reduced motion.
openai_fund_angle: Make OpenAI usage visible and useful. The landing page and README name the real models (gpt-realtime as a voice option, gpt-4.1-mini for coaching and grading). Each session footer shows models used with a token and cost meter, and Settings offers a model swap with a note on what changes. Wizard drafts carry a 'Generated with GPT' badge. For contributors: a 'Good first persona' board, a 'Build a pack with Codex' button that opens a pre-filled Codex task, and a contributor wall with merged pack counts. Pack PRs run a Codex review checklist, which gives a concrete Codex-for-Open-Source PR-review story.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about 1 week): upgrade to Tailwind v4 and add HeroUI v3 beside existing components, mapping tokens to :root. Phase 1: shell, navigation, landing and README hero. Phase 2: library data model (JSON packs) and filters, then the wizard. Phase 3: pre-call brief and live call with the three lanes, whispers and live rubric. Phase 4: debrief replay, progress and manager views. Phase 5: mobile call and dark-mode polish. Each phase ships behind a flag, and current pages stay live until parity.

risks: HeroUI v3 is new and has dropped Framer Motion; API churn or the Tailwind v4 migration could stall Phase 0.
Coach and grader latency must stay under about 1.5 seconds or whispers feel late; needs a fallback to turn-end scoring.
Content load: 150 quality personas is a large writing task. Ship about 60 reviewed and label the rest 'community draft'.
Crowded market: Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli, Outdoo AI and Mindtickle already ship live or real-call coaching. The open-source core must lead on transparency and evidence.
Voice cloning and real-person likeness must stay opt-in with consent, and avatars stay illustrated.
Soft HeroUI defaults can look like every AI SaaS; the custom palette and coach rail are what keep it distinct.
Cost: coach lane, grader and Realtime voice multiply per-call spend. The cost meter must be honest and the default models the cheapest that pass evaluation.
